messages:
Sam (platform): heads-up — GreenPay reported a routing flap this morning. Their old proxy sometimes injects duplicate headers and shoves a compression token into the end of the User-Agent string, which breaks our UA-based routing heuristics. Anyone seen this pattern before?
Priya (eng-infra): yep, saw similar from an on-prem partner last quarter. legacy proxies will comma-join and sometimes append flags.
Alex (runtime): we should normalize header lists and trim trailing tokens before matching. also consider a signed-assertion short-circuit for guaranteed routing.
Maria (security): agree on signed assertions. if we trust X-Redwood-Route-Sig and it verifies, that should override heuristics. we need clear audit logs when we accept/ignore it.
Sam (platform): quick dump of what we're seeing from GreenPay: 
```
GET /api/generate
Host: api.redwood.com
User-Agent: GreenPayClient/2.1.0 gzip
X-Forwarded-For: 10.1.2.3, 203.0.113.45
X-Tenant-Hint: tenant_abc
X-Redwood-Route-Sig: <signed-blob>
```
Priya (eng-infra): that `gzip` suffix is the problem for our current regex. we either strip common compression tokens or anchor the regex to the start. strip list sounds safer.
Alex (runtime): proposal (fast, minimal change): canonicalize UA by removing tokens matching `/ (gzip|brotli|deflate) /i` and collapse runs of whitespace. then run existing UA match. Fallback order: signed-sig -> X-Tenant-Hint -> UA -> client-meta.
Maria (security): +1 but add signature verification TTL (max 5m) and key-id check. documented fallback MUST record reason in trace logs: `route_decision_reason`.
Priya (eng-infra): also watch for header merging where proxies comma-join tenant hints: `X-Tenant-Hint: tenant_abc, tenant_x` — prefer left-most non-empty after trim.
Sam (platform): thinking about console UX — should we surface a per-request `route_decision` column in the trace table? quick toggle to show raw headers + normalized headers?
Alex (runtime): please yes. it helps debugging. small perf hit if we store raw headers for every request, maybe sample 1% by default and 100% when debug flag set.
Maria (security): sampling ok, but for routes where signed assertions are used, keep 100% audit for at least 24h.
Priya (eng-infra): implementation note: edge proxy will run normalization filter. runtime will consume `X-Redwood-Canonical-UA` and `X-Redwood-Route-Decision`. that keeps mutation surface small.
Sam (platform): rough canary plan: ship normalization + console toggle to dedicated customers first, monitor `route_mismatch_rate` and `console_support_tickets`. roll to general after 48h stable. anyone object?
Alex (runtime): no objections. I'll open RFC with the regex and pseudocode.
Priya (eng-infra): i'll add the sampling + retention config to infra checklist.
Maria (security): add a note in the rollout doc to contact security for any exceptions where proxies intentionally mangle headers.
infra-bot: deploybot: created issue PLAT-8423 to track UA normalization RFC and rollout.
Sam (platform): thanks — if you can all reply with thumbs-up on PLAT-8423 I'll start the canary tomorrow morning. :thumbsup:
